title: Practical exams & capstone
theory: This companion records your practice and evidence. Browser quiz answers and imported local results are inspectable and editable. No score here is a proctored assessment or an official Harvard credential.

For an independent attempt, documentation is allowed. Tailored hints, generated implementation, or a viewed solution make the attempt assisted. Record this honestly; the platform cannot observe outside assistance.

A rebuild task is a new problem using the same concepts. To count as retained evidence here, pass it independently at least 48 hours after an earlier independent build. That is a practice rule, not a scientific threshold for universal mastery.

An unfamiliar person should be able to follow your setup instructions, run the program, and reproduce the tests. State limitations openly. Keep the portfolio made of code and evidence rather than decorative progress percentages.

quiz.prompt: What is the strongest evidence among these for application skill?
quiz.explanation: An inspectable artifact with tests demonstrates more than exposure.

quiz.prompt: A local report is imported successfully. Does that prove no help was used?
quiz.explanation: The report is not a proctor and cannot establish independence.

quiz.prompt: Documentation-only work under this companion's rules is?
quiz.explanation: Reference documentation is allowed; tailored solutions and hints are treated separately.

quiz.prompt: A practical requirement is unclear. Best engineering response?
options: Document an explicit assumption and its consequences
quiz.explanation: Make assumptions inspectable and test the chosen contract.

options: Setup instructions, pinned dependencies, sample data, and tests
quiz.explanation: Another person needs the environment and procedure as well as the source.

quiz.prompt: A bug appears after a change. What should be added after repairing it?
quiz.explanation: A regression test protects the repaired behavior from recurring.

tasks.title: Midterm practical: C toolkit
tasks.brief: Complete a cumulative C assignment from specifications, not a tutorial.
requirements: Create a CLI that stores up to 100 fictional measurement records, searches them, and prints sorted summaries.
Combine arrays, functions, conditionals, loops, and an explicit search/sort algorithm.
Write at least eight tests, including missing records and boundary sizes.
Suggested 90-minute practice window; documentation allowed. Report assistance and elapsed time yourself.

rubric: Meets every written requirement, not only the example.

tasks.title: Capstone: your technician toolkit
tasks.brief: Deliver the evolving project as a coherent application.
requirements: Include a usable interface, Python/Flask logic, SQLite persistence, and at least one reusable calculation tool.
Use only synthetic data and document any security or deployment gaps.
Provide a versioned repository, sample data, pinned dependencies, setup steps, and tests.
Explain three design decisions, three repaired defects, and one requirement change you handled independently.
Demonstrate the application and list which capabilities are supported by automated checks versus self-review.
